title: Situational writing (SG)
examples: When should I use a formal tone versus an informal tone?
How does knowing the audience change my writing style?
Can you give me an example of writing for a specific purpose?

explain.say: Today we are learning about situational writing. This means writing for a specific situation.
First we must consider the purpose of our writing. What do you want the reader to do after reading it?
Next we need to think about the audience. Who exactly are you writing this piece for? You must know them.
The context is the background setting for your writing. Where and when are you writing this piece?
Task fulfilment means making sure you have done everything the task asks. Did you include all the required parts?

draw.text: Task Fulfilment: Did you meet all requirements?

explain.say: For a real-life example, imagine you need to write an email to the school principal. Your purpose is to request a change to the library hours. You must use a formal tone because of the audience and the context.

items: Row 2: Formal Greeting | Clear Request | Formal Sign-off

faq.q: How important is the audience when I write something?
faq.a: The audience is very important because it controls your tone and vocabulary. If you write for children, you use simple words, but if you write for experts, you use technical terms.
asks: Does who I write to change my words?
Should I change my style based on the reader?

faq.q: What is the difference between purpose and context?
faq.a: The purpose is your goal, like to inform. The context is the surrounding situation, like writing during a school assembly. Both help guide your writing.
asks: Are purpose and context the same thing?
Do I need both purpose and context?

faq.q: If I forget the context, what happens to my writing?
faq.a: Your writing might sound strange or inappropriate for the situation. For example, using slang in a job application would be wrong.
asks: Can I write without knowing the setting?
What if the context is confusing?

faq.q: How do I make sure I have fulfilled the task?
faq.a: You should read the instructions carefully and check off every single requirement listed. If it asks for three paragraphs, make sure you have three.
asks: How do I check if I did everything?
What is task fulfilment in writing?

faq.q: Can I use a mix of formal and informal language?
faq.a: It is best to stick to one tone. Mixing them can confuse the reader and make your writing seem unclear or unprofessional.
asks: Is it okay to sound casual sometimes?

facts: Purpose answers the question: Why am I writing this?
Audience answers the question: Who is reading this?
Context answers the question: Where and when is this happening?
Task fulfilment means meeting every requirement given in the prompt.

quiz.say: You are writing a notice for the school notice board to remind students about the upcoming sports day. Your primary purpose is to:
quiz.why: The notice needs to give factual details, which is the purpose of informing.

wrong.0: The context is an official notice, so the tone must be serious and factual.
wrong.1: The audience is the whole school, so the tone must be neutral and official.
wrong.3: This is too strong; the notice should just state the facts, not try to convince them.

quiz.say: You are writing a letter to your best friend about a movie you saw last night. Which element should guide your vocabulary and tone?

options.show: Language suitable for a newspaper article.
options.say: Language suitable for a newspaper article.

quiz.why: Since the audience is a close friend, you can use casual language.

wrong.1: This would sound unnatural and overly stiff for a friend.
wrong.2: Your friend will not understand specialized terms used by critics.
wrong.3: The setting is private, so a public style does not fit the context.

quiz.say: A science textbook chapter on photosynthesis is written for Year 9 students. If you write a summary for this chapter, what must you remember about task fulfilment?

options.show: Change the scientific terminology to be simpler.
options.say: Change the scientific terminology to be simpler.

options.show: Write a story about a plant growing.
options.say: Write a story about a plant growing.

options.show: You must cover the main stages mentioned in the textbook.
options.say: You must cover the main stages mentioned in the textbook.

options.show: Add your own personal opinions about plants.
options.say: Add your own personal opinions about plants.

quiz.why: The task is to summarize, so you must include the core, factual points from the source material.

wrong.0: While simplifying is good, you must keep the core scientific terms accurate to the source.
wrong.1: The task requires summarizing facts, not creating a fictional narrative.
wrong.3: The task is to summarize the textbook, not to give a personal review.
